header.userPrompt:
Add a new "set category" rule type to the bank-statement-row rule system. Today a rule can "set a merchant" (`set_merchant`) or "ignore" (`ignore`) a row, matched against the row description. Add a third action `set_category` that resolves ONLY a category (no merchant) for matching rows — e.g. a description containing "CAFETERIA" maps to the "Snacks" category.

The entire rule system is small and centralized; the file:line insertion points below were confirmed by exploration against the current `main`. Keep the change surgical and follow existing patterns exactly.

## Priority / matching semantics (MOST IMPORTANT — get this exactly right)

All priority logic is in `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/ImportRuleMatcher.scala`. Matching is substring/contains on a normalized string (`normalize` = lowercase + strip non-alphanumeric), with `MinPatternLength = 3`. Within a group of rules, `findWinner` picks the longest normalized pattern, tiebreak = latest UUIDv7 id.

Today `findRowWinner` (around lines 41-47) tiers action groups via `orElse`:
```scala
val ignoreWinner   = findWinner(matched.filter(_.action == ImportRuleAction.Ignore))
val merchantWinner = findWinner(matched.filter(_.action == ImportRuleAction.SetMerchant))
ignoreWinner.orElse(merchantWinner)
```
Add a third group and chain it LAST so the tier order becomes **ignore > set_merchant > set_category**:
```scala
val categoryWinner = findWinner(matched.filter(_.action == ImportRuleAction.SetCategory))
ignoreWinner.orElse(merchantWinner).orElse(categoryWinner)
```
This means a set_merchant rule ALWAYS beats a set_category rule when both match, regardless of pattern length (e.g. "CAFE" as set_merchant beats "CAFETERIA" as set_category); within the same action group, the longest pattern still wins. Do NOT change the longest-pattern-wins logic inside `findWinner`.

`effectiveRules` (virtual per-merchant SetMerchant rules) must stay unchanged — set_category rules are always explicit/stored, never virtual.

## Decisions already made (do NOT deviate)
- **(1A) A set_category-matched row is fully resolved by the rule** (category set, merchant left blank) and is **excluded from the AI suggestion engine**, exactly like a set_merchant- or ignore-matched row. Do not send it to AI, and do not attempt partial (merchant-only) AI resolution for it.
- **(2A) Rule creation from a statement row is OPT-IN via a checkbox** in the confirm form, mirroring the existing set_merchant alias UX — never auto-create silently.

## Area 1 — DB (new evolution)
Highest existing evolution is `9.sql`; add `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/10.sql`. The `merchant_rule` table is defined in `3.sql` (columns: id, user_id, pattern CITEXT, action TEXT, merchant_id UUID nullable, auto_created, created_at, updated_at; partial unique indexes for ignore and set_merchant).

Add to `merchant_rule`:
- `category_id UUID` nullable column
- FK `merchant_rule_category_id_fk FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES category(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (category PK is `category(id)`)
- index `merchant_rule_category_id_index` on `(category_id)`
- partial unique index `merchant_rule_set_category_unique` on `(user_id, pattern, category_id) WHERE action = 'set_category'`

Follow Play Evolutions conventions in this repo: only a `# --- !Ups` section (NO `!Downs`), auto-applied, contiguous numbering, and **no semicolons inside SQL comments** (Play splits on `;`). Do NOT add CHECK constraints (app-level validation only — matches the existing free-text `action` column).

## Area 2 — shared ADT + models
- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/merchants/ImportRuleAction.scala`: add `case object SetCategory extends ImportRuleAction("set_category")` and include it in `values`. JSON `Format` and Tapir `Schema` are string-based and need no other change.
- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/ImportRuleMatcher.scala`: add `categoryId: Option[UUID]` to the `Rule` case class (alongside `merchantId`).
- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/RowRuleVerdict.scala`: add a `final case class SetCategory(categoryId: Option[UUID]) extends Verdict`, and update `verdict(...)` — the current catch-all `case Some(w) =>` (around line 19-20) maps any non-ignore winner to `SetMerchant`; change it to explicitly branch on `w.action`: `SetMerchant` -> `SetMerchant(w.merchantId)`, `SetCategory` -> `SetCategory(w.categoryId)`. Keep `ruleMerchantId` returning the merchantId only for SetMerchant winners; add a parallel `ruleCategoryId` helper that returns the categoryId for a SetCategory winner (and, where it already derives category from a matched merchant, leave that path intact).

## Area 3 — server persistence
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/models/ImportRule.scala`: add `categoryId: Option[UUID]` and `categoryName: Option[String]` to `ImportRule`, and `categoryId: Option[UUID]` to `ImportRule.Create`.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/daos/ImportRuleDAO.scala`: add `category_id` to the INSERT (`create`) and UPDATE (`update`); add `category_id` + a LEFT JOIN on `category` to the SELECTs (`all`, `find`) to populate `categoryName`; extend `ruleParser` to read `category_id` and `category_name`. Add an `existsByUserPatternCategory(userId, pattern, categoryId)` dup-check method parallel to `existsByUserPatternMerchant`.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/ImportRuleRepository.scala`: thread `categoryId` through `create` (keep UUIDv7 id generation).
- chimney `transformInto[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]` conversions (e.g. `ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction`, `TelegramExpenseAction`, `ParseReceiptAction`) should pick up the new `categoryId` field automatically since the field name matches; verify they compile.

## Area 4 — API endpoints + actions
- Request/response models under `lib/api/shared/.../models/merchants/`: add `categoryId: Option[UUID]` to `CreateImportRule.Request` and `UpdateImportRule.Request`; add `categoryId: Option[UUID]` and `categoryName: Option[String]` to `GetImportRules.Rule`.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/importrules/CreateImportRuleAction.scala` and `UpdateImportRuleAction.scala`: add a `SetCategory` branch — validate `normalize(pattern).length >= MinPatternLength`, require `categoryId` present and the category exists & is user-owned (follow how `SetMerchant` validates the merchant), require `merchantId` empty, run the `existsByUserPatternCategory` dup-check, then create/update with `category_id`.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/importrules/GetImportRulesAction.scala`: map the new fields into `GetImportRules.Rule`.
- No new endpoints; reuse the existing `/import-rules` CRUD.

## Area 5 — AI suggestion engine (enforce decision 1A)
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/StatementSuggestionsService.scala` (`selectRowsToResolve`, ~168-177): it already excludes rows whose `RowRuleVerdict.verdict != NoRule`. Since a set_category match now yields a `SetCategory` verdict (not `NoRule`), those rows are automatically excluded from AI — confirm this holds and add/adjust a test. Do not special-case anything to re-include them.

## Area 6 — frontend
Adding `SetCategory` to the ADT will break every exhaustive `match`/selector on the two current actions — fix each:
- `web/.../components/pages/ImportRulesPage.scala`: add a "Set category" option to the action selector (~221-237), show a category autocomplete when SetCategory is selected (reuse the merchant-autocomplete pattern but for categories), send `categoryId` on create/update, and display set_category rules as `→ <categoryName>` in the rule row (~326-394).
- `web/.../components/pages/BankRowRuleForm.scala`: add `SetCategory` to the action select (~183-208); it already has a category autocomplete (~162-181) — wire it to build a `set_category` rule when that action is chosen.
- `web/.../components/pages/BankRowCreateExpenseForm.scala`:
  - Prefill: when the row's rule winner is a `SetCategory` verdict, prefill the category from the rule and leave the merchant blank (extend `initialSelection`, ~42-65).
  - Creation on confirm (~285-309): today it creates a set_merchant alias rule when `hint == NeedsAlias` and a merchant resolved. Add a parallel path: when the row is confirmed with a **category chosen but NO merchant**, and gated behind a NEW opt-in checkbox (label e.g. "Also categorize similar rows as <category>"), POST a `CreateImportRule.Request(action = SetCategory, pattern = <alias/description>, categoryId = Some(catId))`. Reuse the existing alias pattern derivation (normalized, >= MinPatternLength). The checkbox should only appear when category-without-merchant applies.
- `web/.../components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala`: `resolveImport` (~96-125) currently derives category only from a matched merchant's categoryId or AI; add the set_category winner as a category source (no merchant). Update the manual `ImportRuleMatcher.Rule(...)` construction (~298) to pass `categoryId`.
- Any other exhaustive matches the compiler flags (e.g. `BulkMerchantSetupPage`, receipts display) — handle minimally; receipts only use SetMerchant winners (`findReceiptWinner`), so set_category must NOT affect the receipt path.

## Frontend reachability / conventions (from repo CLAUDE.md)
- Scala.js/Slinky/MUI conventions: use `def` (not `val`) for reused React elements; component tests use `BrowserRouter` + jsdom; object-level `val`s only plain JS literals.
- All DB queries keep `WHERE user_id = ?`; list queries keep a stable `ORDER BY`.
- Tapir endpoint/model changes go in `lib/api/shared/`, never `server/`.
- CI runs with `-Werror`; `apiJS/compile` and `web/compile` must pass.

## Area 7 — tests
- `lib/api/shared/src/test/.../ImportRuleMatcherSpec.scala` and `RowRuleVerdictSpec.scala`: cover the new tier — set_merchant beats set_category even when the category pattern is longer ("CAFE" set_merchant vs "CAFETERIA" set_category -> merchant wins); set_category wins when it is the only/longest matching non-merchant rule; ignore still beats both.
- `server/src/test/.../ImportRulesControllerSpec.scala` and `ImportRuleRepositorySpec.scala`: create/list/update/delete a set_category rule; validation (category must exist & be user-owned, merchantId must be empty); dup-check.
- A suggestion-service test asserting a set_category-matched debit row is excluded from the AI resolve set (decision 1A).
- Web specs: extend `ImportRuleListSpec.scala`, `BankStatementReviewPageSpec.scala`, `BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec.scala` to cover the set_category display/selector and the opt-in rule-creation checkbox (category-without-merchant on confirm).

## Pre-PR sequence (repo CLAUDE.md)
`CI=true sbt Test/compile` → `git add` → `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` (re-stage reformatted) → `CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test` (foreground, must exit 0) → open PR. Keep the change limited to what this feature needs; do not refactor unrelated code or prune existing rules.

## Success criteria
1. A `set_category` rule can be created/listed/updated/deleted via the rules UI and the row rule form, carrying a category (no merchant).
2. Matching honors the tier order ignore > set_merchant > set_category, with longest-pattern-wins inside each tier (verified by the "CAFE vs CAFETERIA" test).
3. A row matched by a set_category rule prefills its category (merchant blank) and is excluded from AI suggestions.
4. Confirming a statement row that has a category but no merchant offers an opt-in checkbox that creates a set_category rule.
5. Full test suite passes; `web/compile` and `apiJS/compile` clean under -Werror.

resultJson.description:
Add a third bank-statement-row import-rule action, `set_category`, alongside `set_merchant` and `ignore`. A set_category rule matches a row description by the same normalized substring logic and gives the row ONLY a category, with no merchant. For example, a description containing "CAFETERIA" gets the "Snacks" category. Priority is tiered: ignore > set_merchant > set_category. A set_merchant match always beats a set_category match, whatever the pattern lengths. Within one action group the existing longest-pattern-wins rule (tiebreak: newest UUIDv7) still applies. Virtual per-merchant rules (`effectiveRules`) and the receipt path (`findReceiptWinner`) are unchanged. set_category rules are always explicit, stored rules.

The change touches every layer. There is a new Play evolution (10.sql) adding `merchant_rule.category_id` with an FK to `category(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE, an index, and a partial unique index. The shared ADT, matcher and verdict gain a SetCategory case. The server model, DAO, repository and actions get validation (category exists and belongs to the user, merchantId empty, dup-check). The API request and response models gain `categoryId`/`categoryName`. On the frontend, set_category rules become creatable and editable from the Import Rules page and the per-row rule form. The statement review page treats a set_category match as a category source with no merchant.

Two product decisions are fixed. (1A) A row matched by a set_category rule is fully resolved by the rule and is excluded from AI suggestions. It already gets a non-NoRule verdict, so `StatementSuggestionsService.selectRowsToResolve` excludes it; no special-casing. (2A) Creating a set_category rule from a confirmed statement row is opt-in, via a new checkbox in the create-expense form. The checkbox only appears when the row has a category but no merchant. Success means the CAFE-vs-CAFETERIA tier test passes, CRUD works through the UI, prefill and AI exclusion behave as described, and `CI=true sbt Test/compile` plus the targeted specs pass under -Werror.

tasks.description:

- add `CONSTRAINT merchant_rule_category_id_fk FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES category(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
- `CREATE INDEX merchant_rule_category_id_index ON merchant_rule USING BTREE (category_id)`
- `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX merchant_rule_set_category_unique ON merchant_rule (user_id, pattern, category_id) WHERE action = 'set_category'`

Server persistence:

Fix the callers: CreateImportRuleAction passes None, UpdateImportRuleAction passes None for now, and ParseReceiptAction/ConfirmReceiptAction/MarkMerchantAsDuplicateAction pass autoCreated by name, so they still compile.

Tests in `ImportRuleRepositorySpec`:

tasks.title: SetCategory action: shared matcher tier, verdict, API models, server validation
tasks.description:
Shared code (`lib/api/shared/src/main`):
- `ImportRuleAction`: add `case object SetCategory extends ImportRuleAction("set_category")` and include it in `values`.
- `ImportRuleMatcher.Rule`: add `categoryId: Option[UUID] = None` as the last param. `effectiveRules` stays unchanged.
- `findRowWinner`: add `categoryWinner = findWinner(matched.filter(_.action == ImportRuleAction.SetCategory))` and return `ignoreWinner.orElse(merchantWinner).orElse(categoryWinner)`. Update the comment. `findWinner`/`findReceiptWinner` stay unchanged.
- `RowRuleVerdict`: add `final case class SetCategory(categoryId: Option[UUID]) extends Verdict`. `verdict` branches explicitly on `w.action` (Ignore, SetMerchant(w.merchantId), SetCategory(w.categoryId)). Add `ruleCategoryId(rules, description): Option[UUID]`, parallel to `ruleMerchantId`.
- `CreateImportRule.Request` and `UpdateImportRule.Request`: add `categoryId: Option[UUID] = None` as the last field.
- `GetImportRules.Rule`: add `categoryId: Option[UUID]` and `categoryName: Option[String]` after merchantName.

Server:

- `ImportRuleDAO`/`ImportRuleRepository`: add `existsByUserPatternCategory(userId, pattern, categoryId, excludeId = None)`, mirroring existing `existsByUserPatternMerchant` (action = 'set_category').
- `CreateImportRuleAction`/`UpdateImportRuleAction` get a `SetCategory` branch:
  - `merchantId` must be empty, otherwise fail with "set_category rules must not have a merchant".
  - `categoryId` is required, otherwise fail with "set_category rules require a category".
  - Look up `CategoriesRepository.find(categoryId, userId)` (inject it). If missing, fail with "Category not found".
  - Run the dup-check, then create/update with `categoryId`.
  - The existing Ignore/SetMerchant branches pass `categoryId = None`, and Update must pass `request.categoryId` only for SetCategory (None otherwise), so switching a rule's action clears stale ids.
- The pattern-length check is already shared.

Web compile fallout, required under -Werror:
- The four `GetImportRules.Rule -> ImportRuleMatcher.Rule` mapping sites pass `categoryId = r.categoryId`: BankStatementReviewPage:298, BankStatementAutoReconcilePage:95, ReceiptsPage:230, BulkMerchantSetupPage:98.
- Exhaustive `ImportRuleAction` matches in `ImportRulesPage` (handleCreate, handleUpdate, the actionSelector label, the rule-row label) and `BankRowRuleForm` (handleSave, the label) need a SetCategory case.
  - The labels get their final text: "Set category" and `s"→ ${r.categoryName.getOrElse("?")}"`.
  - SetCategory is NOT yet added to the selector item Seqs. The handler branches can set the error "Set category rules are not available here yet", which the next task replaces.
- `ImportRuleListSpec` fixture: add the new GetImportRules.Rule fields.

Tests:
- `ImportRuleMatcherSpec`/`RowRuleVerdictSpec` cover four cases:
  - "CAFE" set_merchant vs "CAFETERIA" set_category on "CAFETERIA CENTRAL": the merchant wins.
  - set_category only: the verdict is `SetCategory(Some(cid))`.
  - The longest pattern wins between two set_category rules.
  - ignore beats both. Also check that `ruleCategoryId`/`ruleMerchantId` return the right values.
- `ImportRulesControllerSpec`:
  - create/list (categoryName populated)/update/delete of a set_category rule.
  - Errors for a missing categoryId, an unknown or other user's category, and a merchantId present.
  - Duplicate create and update (excludeId) are rejected.
- `StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec`: `selectRowsToResolve` excludes a debit row matched only by a set_category rule (decision 1A). Do not change the service code.

Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile`, then testOnly `*ImportRuleMatcherSpec *RowRuleVerdictSpec *ImportRulesControllerSpec *ImportRuleRepositorySpec *StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec`.

tasks.title: Opt-in checkbox in BankRowCreateExpenseForm to create a set_category rule on confirm
tasks.description:
In `BankRowCreateExpenseForm`, add a new opt-in checkbox for the case where the row is confirmed with a category but no merchant:
- The checkbox state defaults to false.
- Show it only when all of these hold: `merchantName.isEmpty`, the category input is non-empty, and `hint == RuleHint.NeedsAlias` (no explicit rule already covers the row). `ruleHint` with an empty merchant name already yields NeedsAlias when no explicit rule matches.
- Label: `Also categorize similar rows as <category name>`. Use MUI `FormControlLabel` + `Checkbox`, or whatever checkbox idiom already exists in `web/` (grep for `Checkbox`).
- When the box is checked, show the existing "Rule pattern" TextField (`rulePattern`, default row.description) so the pattern is editable. Helper text: e.g. "Future rows containing this text get this category."

On a successful save:
- Thread `resolvedCategoryId` out of the `fExpense` for-comprehension, alongside expenseId and resolvedMerchantId. This covers a category created inline.
- If resolvedMerchantId is None, the checkbox is checked, the category is defined, and `aliasToCreate(rulePattern, "")` is Some(pattern), POST `CreateImportRule.Request(action = ImportRuleAction.SetCategory, pattern = pattern, merchantId = None, categoryId = Some(catId))`. `aliasToCreate` applies the normalize / MinPatternLength rule.
- On success, call `props.onNewEntities(Some(ImportRuleMatcher.Rule(r.id, SetCategory, pattern, None, Some(catId))), None)` and then `onSuccess`.
- On failure, reuse the existing `setSavedExpenseId` + "Expense created, but the rule could not be created: …" path.
- The existing set_merchant alias path stays unchanged.

Put the decision in a pure helper, e.g. `categoryRuleToCreate(hint, merchantName, categoryIdOpt, optIn, pattern): Option[String]`. Unit-test it in `BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec`:
- With opt-in off, nothing is created.
- With a merchant present, nothing is created.
- When the row is covered by a rule, nothing is created.
- A too-short pattern creates nothing.
- The happy path returns the trimmed pattern.

Add a render-without-crash jsdom test with the checkbox visible only if it guards a real element-reuse risk (RULE-TE-010). No setTimeout or other hacks.

Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
Stack: Scala 3 (enum, `import x.*`, `using`). Play + Tapir backend (`server/`), Anorm DAOs, Play Evolutions (Postgres, testcontainers in tests). Shared cross-built module `lib/api/shared` (JVM + JS). Scala.js + Slinky + MUI 5 frontend (`web/`). `CI=true` turns on -Werror, so a non-exhaustive `match` on the sealed `ImportRuleAction` is a compile ERROR. Chimney is used for `repositories.models.ImportRule -> ImportRuleMatcher.Rule` (`_.transformInto[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]` in ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction:61, TelegramExpenseAction:46, ParseReceiptAction:89). Names must match, and extra source fields are ignored.

KEY FILES
- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/merchants/ImportRuleAction.scala`: `sealed abstract class ImportRuleAction(val entryName: String)`; objects SetMerchant("set_merchant") and Ignore("ignore"); `values: Seq`; `fromEntryName`; string-based Format/Schema.
- `.../models/merchants/CreateImportRule.scala`: `Request(action, pattern: String, merchantId: Option[UUID])`, `Response(id)`. `UpdateImportRule.scala` is similar. `GetImportRules.scala`: `Rule(id, action, pattern, merchantId, merchantName, autoCreated, createdAt, updatedAt)`, `Response(data: List[Rule])`. Play-json `Json.format` reads missing Option fields as None.
- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/ImportRuleMatcher.scala`:
  - `case class Rule(id, action, pattern, merchantId: Option[UUID])`
  - `MinPatternLength = 3`; `normalize` = lowercase + strip [^a-z0-9]
  - `effectiveRules(explicit, merchants: List[(UUID,String)])` adds virtual SetMerchant rules (id = merchant id)
  - `findMatches`; `findWinner` (maxBy (normalized length, id.toString))

resultJson.title: Add set_category import rule action
resultJson.body:
This adds a third action for bank-statement-row import rules: `set_category`. It sits next to `set_merchant` and `ignore`. When a row matches a `set_category` rule, the row gets only a category and no merchant. For example, a description containing "CAFETERIA" maps to "Snacks".

**Matching priority** is now ignore > set_merchant > set_category. A set_merchant match always beats a set_category match, whatever the pattern lengths: a "CAFE" set_merchant rule beats a "CAFETERIA" set_category rule. Within one action, the longest pattern still wins. Virtual per-merchant rules and the receipt path are unchanged, so set_category rules never apply to receipts.

**Changes:**
- **DB:** evolution `10.sql` adds `merchant_rule.category_id`. It has an FK to `category(id)` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so deleting a category deletes its rules. It also adds an index and a partial unique index on `(user_id, pattern, category_id)` for set_category rules.
- **API/server:**
  - Create and update requests take `categoryId`, and list responses include `categoryId` and `categoryName`.
  - set_category rules must have a category that belongs to the user, must not have a merchant, and go through a duplicate check.
  - When an update switches a rule to a different action, its category is cleared.
- **AI suggestions:** a row matched by a set_category rule counts as resolved by the rule, so it is not sent to AI. No service code changed; the existing `NoRule` filter already handles it, and a test covers it.
- **Frontend:**
  - The Import Rules page and the per-row rule form can create and edit set_category rules, using a category autocomplete.
  - The review page uses a set_category match as the row's category with no merchant. The create-expense form prefills that category and leaves the merchant input blank, so saving doesn't create a merchant named after the description.
  - When a row is confirmed with a category but no merchant, a new opt-in checkbox "Also categorize similar rows as <category>" creates a set_category rule. Nothing is created unless the user ticks it.
- **Small refactor:** the category resolve-or-create logic is pulled into `DescriptionRow.resolveOrCreateCategory` and reused by the forms. `ImportRuleMatcher.Rule.fromApi` replaces the repeated mapping from API rules.
